packages.name: vm_service
packages.description: A library to communicate with a service implementing the Dart VM service protocol.
packages.oneLiner: A library to communicate with a service implementing the Dart VM service protocol.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Dart client library to communicate with the Dart VM service protocol. It allows developers to interact with running Dart and Flutter virtual machines for debugging and inspection purposes.
useWhen: Building debugging tools or developer extensions for Dart and Flutter
Interacting directly with the Dart VM service protocol programmatically
avoidWhen: Building standard application features unrelated to debugging or VM inspection
strengths: Official library for communicating with the Dart VM service
Kept up-to-date with Dart VM service protocol specifications
weaknesses: Low-level protocol client which requires deep understanding of the Dart VM service spec

packages.name: analyzer
packages.description: This package provides a library that performs static analysis of Dart code.
packages.oneLiner: Performs static analysis of Dart code for tool integration and embedding.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a library for performing static analysis on Dart code. It allows developers to configure analysis options, examine elements, and build custom IDE tools, formatters, or documentation generators.
useWhen: You are building a custom Dart tool or editor integration
You need to programmatically analyze Dart source code and inspect elements
avoidWhen: You just want to run standard linting on your project (use the built-in `dart analyze` command instead)
You are an end-user looking for a command-line analysis tool
strengths: Powers major Dart tooling like dart format and dart doc
Supports fine-grained analysis options and custom lint rules
weaknesses: APIs were originally machine generated from a Java implementation and may not feel like clean Dart APIs
No clean distinction currently between public and internal APIs, leading to potential breaking changes
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml and optionally configure an analysis_options.yaml file in your project root.

packages.name: archive
packages.description: Provides encoders and decoders for various archive and compression formats such as zip, tar, bzip2, gzip, zlib, xz, and zstd.
packages.oneLiner: Encodes and decodes archive and compression formats such as zip, tar, gzip, and zlib.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides encoders and decoders for various archive and compression formats. It handles reading and writing zip, tar, bzip2, gzip, zlib, xz, and zstd formats both in memory and via streaming.
useWhen: You need to read or write zip and tar archives within a Dart or Flutter app.
You need to decompress or compress data using formats like GZip, ZLib, BZip2, XZ, or Zstandard.
avoidWhen: You are running on the web platform and need to use InputFileStream for local file system access.
strengths: Supports a wide variety of compression and archive formats.
Provides stream-based APIs and memory-efficient file streaming to minimize memory usage.
weaknesses: File system operations like InputFileStream are not supported on the web platform.

packages.name: yaml
packages.description: A parser for YAML, a human-friendly data serialization standard
packages.oneLiner: A Dart library for parsing YAML documents into Dart data structures.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to load YAML strings or streams into Dart objects. It supports error recovery and detailed error reporting. The library does not support dumping YAML back to text.
useWhen: Parsing configuration files in Dart or Flutter apps
Converting YAML data to Dart maps/lists for further processing
Reading YAML from network or local files
avoidWhen: When you need to generate YAML output
When working with very large YAML files that require streaming parsing
strengths: Pure Dart implementation, no native dependencies
Supports error recovery with custom listeners
Maintained by dart-lang with regular updates
Compatible with all platforms (web, mobile, desktop)
weaknesses: No YAML dumping support
Limited to parsing, not editing or serializing
Some edge cases (self-referential collections) still throw exceptions

packages.name: meta
packages.description: Annotations used to express developer intentions that can't otherwise be deduced by statically analyzing source code.
packages.oneLiner: Annotations to express developer intentions for static analysis tools.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides annotations like @visibleForTesting, @immutable, and @sealed that static analysis tools use to analyze source code and check developer intentions. It also includes experimental annotations for dart2js.
useWhen: You want to guide the Dart analyzer with custom metadata on classes, methods, or variables.
You are writing code that requires strict enforcement of architectural intentions such as mustCallSuper or immutable.
avoidWhen: You need a general-purpose state management or UI library.
You are looking for runtime dependency injection frameworks.
strengths: Officially maintained by the Dart team.
Zero dependencies.
Directly integrates with the Dart analyzer and IDE warnings.
weaknesses: Provides only annotations and no runtime logic or utilities.
Some hints/annotations may be experimental or change between minor versions.
explainer.setupNotes: Add package to dependencies in pubspec.yaml.

packages.name: pub_semver
packages.description: Versions and version constraints implementing pub's versioning policy. This is very similar to vanilla semver, with a few corner cases.
packages.oneLiner: Versions and version constraints implementing pub's versioning policy.

explainer.whatItDoes: Implements parsing, comparison, and constraint checking for semantic version numbers according to pub's specific versioning policy. It handles special pub corner cases like build suffix ordering and pre-release prioritization.
useWhen: You need to parse and compare semantic version numbers in Dart
You are building tools that deal with pub-compatible package version constraints
avoidWhen: You are looking for vanilla semver without pub's specific pre-release and build suffix policies
strengths: Matches pub's exact versioning and constraint policy
Handles complex ranges, unions, and pre-release priority rules
weaknesses: Not strictly compliant with vanilla SemVer 2.0.0 in certain corner cases due to pub-specific policies

packages.name: uuid
packages.description: RFC4122 (v1, v4, v5, v6, v7, v8) UUID Generator and Parser for Dart
packages.oneLiner: Generates and parses RFC‑4122/9562 UUIDs (v1‑v8) for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to create version‑1,‑4,‑5,‑6,‑7 and‑8 UUIDs and to validate or parse 128‑bit hexadecimal strings. Works on all Dart platforms with cryptographically strong RNG by default.
useWhen: You need unique identifiers across devices or services
You require support for newer UUID versions (v6‑v8) or strict RFC validation
avoidWhen: You need a UUID library with built‑in persistence or database integration
You prefer a code‑gen based solution for IDs
strengths: Cryptographically strong random generation on all platforms
Supports the full range of RFC‑4122 and RFC‑9562 versions
Provides explicit format validation and parsing utilities
weaknesses: Only focuses on UUID generation/parsing – no storage or networking features
No code‑generation helpers; you must call the API directly

packages.name: mime
packages.description: Utilities for handling media (MIME) types, including determining a type from a file extension and file contents.
packages.oneLiner: Utilities to resolve MIME types from file names, magic bytes, and to parse multipart streams.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to look up a MIME type based on a filename or header bytes and to get a file extension from a MIME type. Includes a stream transformer that splits multipart/form-data into separate parts.
useWhen: You need to determine MIME types for files without external libraries
You need to parse multipart/form-data streams in a server or client
You want a lightweight, pure‑Dart solution for MIME handling
avoidWhen: You require a full‑featured HTTP client that already handles multipart parsing
You need advanced MIME type detection beyond extensions and basic magic numbers
strengths: Zero dependencies, pure Dart
Supports both extension and magic‑byte lookup
Provides a ready‑to‑use multipart stream transformer
weaknesses: Limited to the built‑in MIME table; not exhaustive for obscure types
No async API for large file scanning beyond header bytes

packages.name: crypto
packages.description: Implementations of SHA, MD5, and HMAC cryptographic functions.
packages.oneLiner: Provides SHA, MD5, and HMAC hashing functions for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Implements common cryptographic hash algorithms (SHA‑1/224/256/384/512, MD5) and HMAC support. All code is pure Dart and works on every Flutter platform.
useWhen: You need to compute hashes or HMACs locally in a Dart/Flutter app.
You require a lightweight, pure‑Dart solution without native dependencies.
avoidWhen: You need audited, security‑certified cryptography.
You require algorithms not provided (e.g., Argon2, RSA).
strengths: Pure Dart, no native dependencies
Supports a wide range of hash functions and HMAC
Works on all Flutter platforms
Performance improvements in recent versions
weaknesses: Not reviewed by security professionals
Limited to hashing/HMAC, no encryption or key management
May lack the latest cryptographic primitives

packages.name: stack_trace
packages.description: A package for manipulating stack traces and printing them readably.
packages.oneLiner: Provides parsing, inspection, and readable formatting of Dart stack traces.

explainer.whatItDoes: The package can convert native StackTrace objects into Trace objects, format them into human‑readable strings, and capture asynchronous stack chains. It also offers utilities like terse formatting to collapse core library frames.
useWhen: You need clearer error logs during development or production debugging
You want to track asynchronous call stacks across zones
You need to format stack traces for reporting or logging
avoidWhen: You only need simple stack traces and want to avoid extra dependencies
Your app size constraints are extremely tight and you cannot afford any extra package
strengths: Produces concise, readable stack traces
Supports asynchronous stack chain capture
Works on all Dart platforms
No code generation required
weaknesses: Adds runtime overhead when capturing chains
Limited to stack‑trace manipulation; not a full logging solution

alternatives.name: logging
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides general logging facilities but lacks stack‑trace parsing and chain features

packages.name: glob
packages.description: A library to perform Bash-style file and directory globbing.
packages.oneLiner: A file and directory globbing library that supports Bash-style path matching and listing.

explainer.whatItDoes: Performs Bash-style file and directory globbing in Dart. It allows developers to check whether a path matches a specific pattern, or recursively list filesystem entities matching a glob pattern using POSIX path syntax.
useWhen: You need to filter files or paths using wildcards like `*` or `**`
You want to recursively list files in a directory matching specific extensions or patterns
avoidWhen: You only need basic path manipulation provided natively by `package:path`
You need complex recursive directory traversal without glob pattern matching
strengths: Supports familiar Bash-style glob syntax including wildcards, character ranges, and option expansion
Works consistently across cross-platform environments using POSIX path syntax
Integrates seamlessly with `package:file` for filesystem operations
weaknesses: Combinatorial option expansions exceeding 10,000 branches will throw a FormatException
Requires using specific imports or a FileSystem object for filesystem listing APIs since version 2.0.0
explainer.setupNotes: none

packages.name: xml
packages.description: Full-featured XML for Dart — DOM parsing, SAX streaming, XPath 3 querying, and a fluent builder API.
packages.oneLiner: Full-featured XML and XPath library for DOM parsing, SAX streaming, and fluent building.

explainer.whatItDoes: Dart XML provides tools for parsing, traversing, querying via XPath 3.1, and building XML documents. It supports both in-memory DOM manipulation and memory-efficient event-driven SAX streaming.
useWhen: You need to parse, query, or manipulate XML documents in Dart or Flutter.
You require XPath 3.1 support for complex document queries.
You need to process large XML streams efficiently without buffering the entire tree.
avoidWhen: You need strict XML Schema (XSD) validation built directly into the parser.
You require full XSLT transformations or complex XQuery modules.
strengths: Comprehensive W3C XPath 3.1 implementation and DOM model.
Supports both pull- and push-based event-driven SAX streaming.
Zero overhead and fully portable across Dart VM, Flutter, and Web.
weaknesses: Does not validate documents against XML Schema (XSD) definitions.
External DTD entity resolution and validation are not enforced.

packages.name: pool
packages.description: Manage a finite pool of resources. Useful for controlling concurrent file system or network requests.
packages.oneLiner: Manage a finite pool of resources to control concurrent operations.

explainer.whatItDoes: The pool package exposes a Pool class that makes it easy to manage a limited pool of resources. It controls concurrent file system or network requests through withResource or fine-grained PoolResource management.
useWhen: You need to limit concurrent file system or network requests.
You want to process an iterable asynchronously with a maximum concurrency limit.
avoidWhen: You are managing state or UI components.
You do not need to limit concurrency.
strengths: Easy to use with withResource callbacks.
Supports fine-grained control via PoolResource objects.
Includes deadlock timeout handling.
weaknesses: Requires manual tracking to ensure physical resources correspond correctly to pool allocations.

packages.name: built_value
packages.description: Value types with builders, Dart classes as enums, and serialization. This library is the runtime dependency.
packages.oneLiner: Immutable value types with builders, enum classes and JSON serialization for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a runtime library to define immutable data models using the builder pattern. Supports enum‑like classes and full JSON (de)serialization, working together with built_collection.
useWhen: You need strongly typed, immutable models with builders
You require robust JSON serialization that handles generics and nested built collections
You want enum‑style classes with additional behavior
avoidWhen: You prefer a lightweight solution without code generation
Your project is small and a simple json_serializable approach is sufficient
strengths: Zero‑runtime reflection – fast and safe
Full support for generics, nested built collections, and custom serializers
Builder pattern enforces immutability and safe updates
weaknesses: Requires build_runner and a generator dev dependency
Steeper learning curve compared to plain json_serializable
Adds extra build step to the CI pipeline
explainer.setupNotes: Add built_value_generator and build_runner as dev_dependencies, then run `dart run build_runner build` (or watch).

alternatives.name: freezed
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides similar immutable data classes with union types and less boilerplate

alternatives.name: json_serializable
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simpler code‑gen for JSON (de)serialization without the builder pattern

packages.name: package_config
packages.description: Support for reading and writing Dart Package Configuration files.
packages.oneLiner: Read and write Dart package configuration files.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides APIs to locate, read, and write .dart_tool/package_config.json files. Offers discovery functions and typed models for package configurations. No longer supports legacy .packages files.
useWhen: You need to resolve package URIs in tooling or build scripts
You are building a Dart tool that must read or modify the package configuration
avoidWhen: You only need simple path manipulation without package resolution
Your project targets Dart versions older than 3.4
strengths: Official API that follows the Dart package config spec
Discovery functions simplify locating config files
Typed models are sealed and ready for future immutability
weaknesses: Only handles package configuration, not a general utility library
Requires Dart 3.4+, so not usable on older SDKs

packages.name: io
packages.description: Utilities for the Dart VM Runtime including support for ANSI colors, file copying, and standard exit code values.
packages.oneLiner: Utilities for the Dart VM Runtime including ANSI colors, file copying, and exit code values.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides helper utilities for Dart VM applications such as ANSI color wrappers for terminal output, file path copying functions, a process manager for spawning subprocesses, and a subscriber-safe wrapper around standard input.
useWhen: You are building a command-line interface (CLI) or Dart VM script that needs terminal colors.
You need to spawn and manage external processes with forwarded I/O streams.
You need to copy directory trees recursively or check if files are executable.
avoidWhen: You are building a Flutter mobile or web application where CLI terminal utilities and process spawning are not applicable.
strengths: Simplifies working with command-line processes and standard input streams.
Provides built-in ANSI coloring helpers for terminal output.
Includes recursive file and directory copying utilities.
weaknesses: Limited to Dart VM environments and does not apply to standard Flutter UI development.
Small feature set focused strictly on specific VM utilities.

packages.name: petitparser
packages.description: Build fast, composable, and type-safe grammars and parsers in Dart.
packages.oneLiner: Build fast, composable, and type-safe grammars and parsers in plain Dart code.

explainer.whatItDoes: PetitParser allows developers to build small, specialized parsers directly in plain Dart code and combine them like LEGO bricks to parse text, configuration values, or complex programming languages. It provides type-safe combinators, character predicates, and transformation methods without requiring external code generators or fragile regular expressions.
useWhen: You need to parse custom text formats, configuration files, or DSLs directly in Dart.
You want a type-safe and composable alternative to complex regular expressions.
You want to build and test grammars in-memory without a separate code-generation step.
avoidWhen: You are parsing simple JSON or formats with widely available dedicated serializers.
You prefer external generator tools (like ANTLR) over code-as-grammar libraries.
strengths: Fully type-safe using modern Dart features and records.
Highly composable with a rich set of combinators and builders.
No external code generators required.
Built-in tools for debugging and viewing execution trees.
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve for developers unfamiliar with parser combinators.
May be overkill for trivial string manipulation tasks.

packages.name: platform
packages.description: A pluggable, mockable platform information abstraction for Dart.
packages.oneLiner: Cross‑platform abstraction for querying runtime platform info in Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a unified API to access native and web platform details, with mock support for tests. It wraps dart:io Platform on native runtimes and exposes browser data on the web.
useWhen: Need to detect OS or browser in a single API
Require testable platform mocks
Build apps that run on multiple Dart platforms without conditional imports
avoidWhen: You only target a single platform and want minimal dependencies
You need advanced device features beyond basic platform info
strengths: Simple, zero‑dependency API
Built‑in test mocking
Supports all major Dart platforms
No code generation required
weaknesses: Limited to platform info only, no device capabilities
Requires manual null checks for web vs native
API changes in 3.2.0 may need migration

alternatives.name: plugin_platform_interface
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a base for platform interfaces but requires custom implementation

alternatives.name: browser_launcher
alternatives.why_pick_it: Only for web browser detection, not cross‑platform

packages.name: dart_style
packages.description: Opinionated, automatic Dart source code formatter. Provides an API and a CLI tool.
packages.oneLiner: Provides an API and CLI to format Dart source code automatically.

explainer.whatItDoes: Rewrites Dart code to follow the official Dart style guide, handling indentation, line wrapping, and punctuation. It can be used as a library or via the `dart format` command.
useWhen: Enforcing consistent code style in a project
Running formatting in CI or pre‑commit hooks
avoidWhen: Needing runtime code transformation
When you require linting beyond formatting
strengths: Official package from the Dart team
Works with the Dart SDK `dart format` command
Configurable via analysis options
weaknesses: Only formats code, no linting or analysis
Limited configuration options

packages.name: clock
packages.description: A fakeable wrapper for dart:core clock APIs.
packages.oneLiner: A fakeable wrapper for dart:core clock APIs.

explainer.whatItDoes: Encapsulates the notion of the current time using a Clock class. Allows swapping out the default top-level clock to reliably test timing-dependent code.
useWhen: You need to test timing-dependent code reliably
You want to mock time or use fake_async for tests
avoidWhen: You only need standard DateTime functionality without mocking or testing requirements
strengths: Integrates seamlessly with the fake_async package
Provides a top-level clock field for default usage
weaknesses: Requires using the wrapper instead of direct dart:core DateTime calls

packages.name: async
packages.description: Utility functions and classes related to the 'dart:async' library.
packages.oneLiner: Utility classes and helpers that extend Dart's async library.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides wrappers, transformers, and helpers for Futures, Streams, and async operations such as caching, memoizing, cancelable operations, and stream grouping. Includes convenience classes like RestartableTimer and Result.
useWhen: You need advanced stream manipulation or cancellation support
You want to cache or memoize expensive async results
avoidWhen: You only need simple async without extra helpers
You require a full state‑management solution
strengths: Rich set of async utilities
Well‑maintained by Dart team
Works on all Dart platforms
weaknesses: Adds extra abstraction layer
May be overkill for tiny projects

packages.name: coverage
packages.description: Coverage data manipulation and formatting
packages.oneLiner: Collects, manipulates, and formats code coverage data in Dart

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides tools to collect coverage JSON from the Dart VM Service and format it into LCOV or pretty-printed formats. Supports ignoring specific lines or ranges from coverage and handling function or branch coverage.
useWhen: You need to generate lcov.info files for test coverage reporting
You want to collect coverage data from the Dart VM Service
You need to filter out ignored lines using coverage comments
avoidWhen: You are looking for a state management or UI library
You do not need test coverage metrics for your Dart project
strengths: Supports LCOV and pretty-printed format output
Supports function and branch coverage collection
Provides comment directives to ignore lines or files from coverage
weaknesses: Web coverage percentage metrics and line counts are not directly comparable to VM runs
explainer.setupNotes: Run dart pub global activate coverage and optionally add the executables to your PATH.
explainer.example: dart pub global run coverage:test_with_coverage

packages.name: source_span
packages.description: Provides a standard representation for source code locations and spans.
packages.oneLiner: Standard representation for source code locations, spans, and human-friendly error messages.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides classes like SourceSpan and SourceFile to track positions in source code files. It allows packages to easily pass code locations around and generate clear, human-friendly error messages with line and column highlights.
useWhen: You are writing a parser, compiler, linter, or code generator that needs to report source code errors.
You want to standardize source location tracking across multiple custom packages.
avoidWhen: You are building a standard mobile application UI without any code parsing requirements.
strengths: Generates clean, human-friendly error messages with file context and line numbers.
Efficient means of computing line and column numbers using SourceFile.
Supports multi-span highlights and Unicode box-drawing characters.
weaknesses: Very niche utility package with no application outside of parsing and tooling.

packages.name: pubspec_parse
packages.description: Simple package for parsing pubspec.yaml files with a type-safe API and rich error reporting.
packages.oneLiner: Parse pubspec.yaml files with a type‑safe API and detailed error reporting.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides classes to read and write pubspec.yaml content, exposing hosted, git, and path dependencies as typed objects. Supports lenient parsing, preserves map spans, and can serialize back to a Map.
useWhen: You need to validate or transform a pubspec.yaml in a tool or CI step
You are building a CLI that inspects package metadata
You want a robust, typed representation of pubspec fields for analysis
avoidWhen: Parsing arbitrary YAML where a generic parser is sufficient
Runtime pubspec parsing in a production Flutter app where size matters
strengths: Typed API for all pubspec fields
Rich, precise error messages via checked_yaml
Supports latest Dart pubspec features (git tag_pattern, falseSecrets, hooks, platforms)
Lenient mode to ignore unknown keys
weaknesses: Specialized to pubspec files only, not a general YAML library
No code‑generation support
Adds another dependency if you already use a generic YAML parser

alternatives.name: yaml
alternatives.why_pick_it: A generic YAML parser that can read any YAML file, including pubspec.yaml, without extra package overhead

packages.name: test_api
packages.description: The user facing API for structuring Dart tests and checking expectations.
packages.oneLiner: The user facing API for structuring Dart tests and checking expectations.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides core APIs for writing and structuring tests in Dart. It supplies the foundational definitions for tests, groups, and expectations.
useWhen: You are building testing tools or libraries that need to hook into the test execution structure.
avoidWhen: You are writing standard unit or integration tests for a Dart or Flutter application (use package:test instead).
strengths: Provides the underlying API required to structure tests and check expectations.
Actively maintained and versioned alongside core testing infrastructure.
weaknesses: Not intended to be publicly used directly for standard application testing.
API may take time to stabilize according to the documentation.

alternatives.name: test
alternatives.why_pick_it: Package:test is the standard and intended package to use for writing and running Dart tests.

packages.name: web
packages.description: Lightweight browser API bindings built around JS interop.
packages.oneLiner: Lightweight bindings for browser APIs via JS interop

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides Dart wrappers around standard web APIs such as document, XMLHttpRequest, WebAssembly, and more. It replaces dart:html for Dart compiled to JS or WASM.
useWhen: Migrating a Dart web app from dart:html to a more modern API
Need direct access to browser APIs in a Dart-only codebase
Want zero‑overhead bindings for web features
avoidWhen: You only need a subset of APIs and prefer a smaller dependency
You are targeting non‑web platforms
strengths: Zero‑overhead, type‑safe bindings
Supports both JS and WASM targets
Actively maintained with migration guides
No build_runner or code generation required
weaknesses: Only works on web platforms
No support for native mobile or desktop APIs
Requires Dart 3.13+
explainer.setupNotes: Add dependency to pubspec and import 'package:web/web.dart';

packages.name: hooks
packages.description: A library that contains a Dart API for the JSON-based protocol for `hook/build.dart` and `hook/link.dart`.
packages.oneLiner: Dart API for the JSON-based protocol for package build and link hooks.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Dart library for writing `hook/build.dart` and `hook/link.dart` scripts to automate building or gathering assets and performing whole-application optimization.
useWhen: You are building or gathering code assets or native binaries for a Dart package
You need to run custom build tasks during a Dart build via hook scripts
avoidWhen: You are developing standard pure-Dart packages that do not require native asset compilation or hooks
strengths: Standardized protocol for native assets and hooks in Dart
Supports user-defines configuration from pubspec.yaml
weaknesses: Niche package restricted to native asset and hook workflows
explainer.setupNotes: Requires setting up build and link scripts within the `hook/` directory of your Dart package.

packages.name: json_annotation
packages.description: Classes and helper functions that support JSON code generation via the `json_serializable` package.
packages.oneLiner: Provides annotations for json_serializable to generate JSON (de)serialization code.

explainer.whatItDoes: Defines annotation classes like @JsonSerializable and @JsonKey that json_serializable reads to produce boilerplate for converting Dart objects to and from JSON. It does not contain any runtime logic itself.
useWhen: You need compile‑time JSON (de)serialization without writing manual toJson/fromJson code.
You are already using json_serializable or want a lightweight annotation package.
avoidWhen: You prefer runtime reflection‑based JSON handling (e.g., json_annotation is not needed).
You target platforms where code generation is not possible.
strengths: Small, zero‑runtime‑overhead package.
Works with Dart 3 and newer SDKs.
Provides fine‑grained control via JsonKey options.

packages.oneLiner: Provides easy access to system information like architecture, kernel, memory, OS, CPU, and user.

explainer.whatItDoes: It retrieves hardware and operating system characteristics such as kernel architecture, bitness, version, operating system name, user details, and memory limits. It allows querying specific host system properties directly in Dart.
useWhen: You need to detect the host operating system or architecture at runtime.
You want to query available physical or virtual memory.
You need user directory or identification details on desktop or mobile environments.
avoidWhen: You need real-time polling of memory in a latency-sensitive UI loop on Windows (as synchronous PowerShell calls can be slow).
PowerShell is disabled or restricted by policy on the target Windows environment.
strengths: Simplifies retrieval of low-level system and hardware details.
Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
weaknesses: Windows memory queries spawn local PowerShell processes which can be slow and are not suited for tight polling loops.
May throw a StateError if Windows PowerShell/CIM fails or is blocked.
explainer.setupNotes: On Windows, PowerShell (powershell.exe) must be available on the PATH with CimCmdlets and local WMI/CIM providers enabled for memory queries.

packages.name: ci
packages.description: Detect whether you're running in a CI environment and information about the CI vendor.
packages.oneLiner: Detect CI environments and inspect CI vendor details in Dart scripts.

You need to detect whether a CI build is running for a pull request.
You want to identify the specific CI vendor hosting your execution environment.

You only need basic platform environment variable lookups without vendor-specific metadata.

packages.name: flutter_dotenv
packages.description: Easily configure any flutter application with global variables using a `.env` file.
packages.oneLiner: Loads configuration variables from .env asset files or strings into Flutter apps.

explainer.whatItDoes: Loads key-value pairs from `.env` files bundled as Flutter assets or parsed from raw strings. Provides typed getters and fallback options to access non-sensitive configuration values like API URLs and feature flags globally. Supports variable interpolation, overriding files, and programmatic merges.
useWhen: You need to manage environment-specific configurations (such as base URLs or log levels) across development, staging, and production
You want a familiar .env syntax with support for variable interpolation and typed values (int, double, bool)
avoidWhen: Storing sensitive secrets like private API keys, tokens, or passwords, because asset files are packaged into the app binary and easily extracted

Handles variable interpolation (`$BASE_URL/v1` and `${BASE_URL}/v1`) natively
weaknesses: Insecure for confidential secrets since asset files are bundled publicly within client builds
Requires `.env` files to be manually registered under the Flutter `assets` section in `pubspec.yaml`

packages.name: mutex
packages.description: Mutual exclusion with implementation of normal and read-write mutex
packages.oneLiner: Mutual exclusion locks and read-write locks for asynchronous Dart code

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides normal mutex and read-write mutex implementations to protect critical sections of code and prevent race conditions when using asynchronous operations. Includes convenience methods like protect, protectRead, and protectWrite to safely acquire and release locks.
useWhen: You have asynchronous operations inside critical sections that risk race conditions
You need multiple read locks to exist simultaneously while restricting write locks to a single exclusive instance
avoidWhen: Your critical section only contains synchronous code, which cannot be interrupted in Dart
Your critical section does not involve shared data or resources accessible by other asynchronous code

Convenience methods ensure locks are always released correctly via try-finally blocks
weaknesses: Requires proper management to avoid deadlocks in complex asynchronous flows

packages.name: flutter_hooks
packages.description: A flutter implementation of React hooks. It adds a new kind of widget with enhanced code reuse.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter implementation of React hooks for managing widget life-cycle and code reuse.

explainer.whatItDoes: It introduces a new kind of object (hooks) that manage the life-cycle of a widget, allowing you to extract and share stateful logic like AnimationControllers across widgets without using complex mixins.
useWhen: You want to share stateful logic across multiple widgets without boilerplate.
You prefer a hooks-based architecture similar to React inside Flutter's build methods.
avoidWhen: You rely heavily on standard StatefulWidget structures and do not want to adopt a hooks paradigm.
You are working with complex conditional hook calls (hooks must be called unconditionally).
strengths: Increases code-sharing between widgets by removing duplicate lifecycle boilerplate.
Extracted logic can be easily packaged and published independently.
weaknesses: Requires strict adherence to rules (calling hooks unconditionally and prefixing with 'use').

explainer.setupNotes: Add as dev_dependency, run `dart pub add --dev build_web_compilers`, create a build.yaml with entrypoint builder configuration, and run `dart run build_runner build`
explainer.example:
```yaml
# build.yaml
targets:
  $default:
    builders:
      build_web_compilers:entrypoint:
        generate_for:
          - web/**.dart
        options:
          compilers:
            dart2js:
              args:
                - O2
            dart2wasm:
              args:
                - O3
```

explainer.example:
Stack(
  children: [
    DropzoneView(
      operation: DragOperation.copy,
      cursor: CursorType.grab,
      onCreated: (DropzoneViewController ctrl) => controller = ctrl,
      onDropFile: (DropzoneFileInterface file) => print('Drop: ${file.webFile}'),

)

explainer.whatItDoes: Allows Flutter applications to programmatically get, set, raise, lower, and mute system volumes. It also provides listeners to detect volume changes in real-time across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and HarmonyOS.
useWhen: You need to build a custom in-app volume slider or control panel.
Your application needs to respond to physical or system volume modifications.
You need to configure Android audio streams or iOS audio session categories.
avoidWhen: You are testing volume control on the iOS simulator, which does not support MPVolumeView.
You are dealing with audio devices like external monitors on desktop that lack volume control support.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and HarmonyOS.
Supports fine-grained features like checking mute status, toggling mute, and setting specific Android audio streams.
weaknesses: Volume controls do not work on the iOS simulator.
Desktop platforms may throw a PlatformException if the default audio device does not support volume control.
explainer.setupNotes: No extra configuration required for basic usage, but follow platform-specific notes if modifying audio session categories or streams.
explainer.example:
await FlutterVolumeController.setVolume(0.5);
final volume = await FlutterVolumeController.getVolume();

flags.label: Native setup
flags.detail: Uses platform code; may need Gradle, Podfile or manifest changes.

packages.name: freerasp
packages.description: Flutter library for improving app security and threat monitoring on Android and iOS mobile devices. Learn more about provided features on the freeRASP's homepage first.
packages.oneLiner: Mobile in-app threat detection, runtime app self-protection, and security monitoring SDK.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides threat detection and security monitoring features for Android and iOS mobile devices. It aims to cover RASP (Runtime App Self Protection) and application shielding aspects like root/jailbreak detection, hook detection, and bootloader checks.
useWhen: You need to detect root or jailbreak attempts on mobile devices.
You want to monitor applications for reverse-engineering or hooking frameworks like Frida.
You require application shielding and threat detection features for Android and iOS.
avoidWhen: You are developing for web or desktop platforms only.
You do not need native application security or threat monitoring features.
strengths: Covers core RASP and application shielding features across Android and iOS.
Detects advanced threats like root/jailbreak, hooking frameworks, and UI automation.
Provides weekly security reports and threat detection insights.
weaknesses: Freemium software with a fair usage policy that imposes limitations on free usage.
Requires specific native setup and configuration steps for Android and iOS integration.
explainer.setupNotes: Requires following platform-specific integration guides for Android and iOS, and handling native dependencies or configuration steps.
explainer.example: not documented

flags.label: Native setup
flags.detail: Uses platform code; may need Gradle, Podfile or manifest changes.

packages.name: amplify_authenticator
packages.description: A prebuilt Sign In and Sign Up experience for the Amplify Auth category
packages.oneLiner: Prebuilt, customizable sign‑in/sign‑up UI for Amplify Auth in Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides an Authenticator widget that handles the full authentication flow, including sign‑in, sign‑up, password reset, and social sign‑in. It manages session state and offers built‑in autofill support.
useWhen: You need a ready‑made authentication UI for Amplify Cognito
You want to reduce boilerplate for auth flows in a Flutter app
You require cross‑platform support (mobile, web, desktop)
avoidWhen: You need a completely custom UI design beyond the provided customization options
You are not using Amplify as your backend
strengths: Zero‑code auth flow integration
Cross‑platform out of the box
Built‑in autofill and accessibility support
Handles session management automatically
weaknesses: Tied to Amplify backend only
Limited to the styling/customization offered by the package
May add bundle size overhead
explainer.setupNotes: Add amplify_auth_cognito, amplify_flutter and amplify_authenticator to pubspec, call Amplify.addPlugin(AmplifyAuthCognito()) and Amplify.configure() before using Authenticator widget.

alternatives.name: amplify_auth_cognito
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer building your own UI on top of the low‑level Cognito plugin

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: When using Firebase as the backend instead of Amplify

alternatives.name: google_sign_in
alternatives.why_pick_it: For simple Google sign‑in without the full Amplify stack

packages.name: dart_ipify
packages.description: This package uses the remote ipify web services in order to get your public IP address or geographical details from any given IP.
packages.oneLiner: Fetch public IP address and geolocation data via the ipify service.

explainer.whatItDoes: The package calls ipify's REST endpoints to return your IPv4/IPv6 address or detailed location info for any IP. It wraps the HTTP calls in simple static methods.
useWhen: You need to quickly obtain the device's public IP address.
You need basic geolocation lookup for an IP without integrating a full mapping SDK.
avoidWhen: You require high‑frequency or bulk IP lookups (rate‑limited by ipify).
You need offline IP resolution or advanced location analytics.
strengths: Very small API surface – just a few async methods.
Works on all major Flutter platforms (mobile, web, desktop).
Null‑safe and actively maintained.
weaknesses: Limited to ipify’s free tier and features.
No built‑in caching or retry logic.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides raw HTTP requests; you can call ipify yourself without an extra wrapper.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: More feature‑rich HTTP client with interceptors and retry support, useful for complex networking needs.

packages.name: beamer
packages.description: A routing package built on top of Router and Navigator's pages API, supporting arbitrary nested navigation, guards and more.
packages.oneLiner: A routing package built on top of Router and Navigator's pages API, supporting arbitrary nested navigation.

explainer.whatItDoes: Beamer splits navigation responsibilities into multiple BeamLocation classes that manage stacks of pages. It integrates with Flutter's Router API to handle deep linking, nested navigation, guards, and browser history synchronization.
useWhen: You need complex, nested routing structures in a Flutter application
You want declarative navigation based on page stacks and URL paths
avoidWhen: You prefer simple imperative navigation like standard Navigator push and pop
You want a zero-configuration routing setup without defining location builders or route maps
strengths: Supports arbitrary nested navigation and multiple beamers
Handles deep linking and browser history out of the box
Allows modular organization of page stacks via BeamLocation
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve compared to imperative navigation or simpler routers
Requires understanding of Router and Navigator 2.0 concepts
explainer.setupNotes: Requires setting up MaterialApp.router with BeamerDelegate, RouteInformationParser, and BeamerBackButtonDispatcher.

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a more declarative URL-based routing API officially recommended by the Flutter team.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers code-generation-based strongly-typed routing and deep-linking support.

flags.label: Quiet but busy
flags.detail: No release in a year while 125 issues are open.

packages.name: navigator_resizable
packages.description: A thin wrapper around Navigator that *visually* resizes the child navigator to match the size of the content displayed in the current route.
packages.oneLiner: A wrapper widget that resizes a child Navigator to match its current route's content size.

explainer.whatItDoes: NavigatorResizable wraps a Navigator and automatically adjusts its size to fit the dimensions of the active route's widget tree. It works with standard Navigator APIs and other routing packages like go_router or auto_route.
useWhen: You need a Navigator that shrinks or grows based on the content of each route
Embedding a Navigator inside a constrained layout (e.g., Dialog, BottomSheet) where size should adapt
avoidWhen: You require unbounded size for the Navigator (e.g., full-screen routes)
Performance‑critical apps where extra layout passes may be costly
strengths: Eliminates manual size calculations for nested navigators
Works with existing navigation APIs and popular routing packages
Handles edge‑case transitions and predictive back gestures
weaknesses: Requires bounded constraints; will assert in debug if parent provides unbounded size
Adds an extra widget layer which may affect performance in very complex hierarchies

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides full routing features including nested navigation without needing a separate resizing wrapper

packages.name: syncfusion_flutter_sliders
packages.description: A Flutter Sliders library for creating highly customizable and UI-rich slider, range slider, and range selector widgets for filtering purposes.
packages.oneLiner: UI-rich slider, range slider, and range selector widgets with numeric and date support.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides native Dart widgets for single value sliders, range sliders, and range selectors that support numeric and date values. Includes rich customization features like tooltips, ticks, labels, and integration with charts.
useWhen: You need standard or vertical sliders and range selectors with numeric or date filtering.
You require advanced features like tooltips, custom tick intervals, and custom label formatting.
avoidWhen: You cannot use a commercial or Syncfusion community license in your project.
You only need a basic Material slider and want to avoid adding a third-party UI library.
strengths: Comprehensive feature set including support for date values, tooltips, ticks, and labels.
Supports both horizontal and vertical orientations along with range selectors and charts integration.
weaknesses: Requires a commercial or Free Syncfusion Community license.
Larger package ecosystem dependency footprint.
explainer.setupNotes: Requires a Syncfusion commercial or community license.

packages.name: youtube_explode_dart
packages.description: A port in dart of the youtube explode library. Supports several API functions without the need of Youtube API Key.
packages.oneLiner: Query YouTube metadata, streams, playlists, captions, and comments without an API key.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Dart interface to query metadata of YouTube videos, playlists, and channels. It resolves and downloads video streams, extracts closed captions, and fetches comments by parsing raw page content and reverse-engineered AJAX requests.
useWhen: You want to fetch YouTube video metadata, captions, or comments without using the official YouTube Data API.
You need to resolve and download YouTube video and audio streams directly.
You are building a custom YouTube downloader or media application in Dart.
avoidWhen: You require guaranteed long-term stability against YouTube's frequent internal web page and API changes.
You need an official, supported Google API with explicit quotas and SLAs.
strengths: No YouTube API key or usage quotas required.
Supports metadata, playlists, comments, captions, and various stream qualities (muxed, audio-only, video-only, HLS).
Allows choosing different YouTube clients and custom signature solvers.
weaknesses: Relies on reverse-engineering and parsing raw page content, making it prone to breaking when YouTube updates its site.
Requires manual cleanup by closing the HTTP client to avoid halting the Dart process.
explainer.setupNotes: Not documented

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want an official widget to play standard video files or network video URLs inside your Flutter application rather than extracting raw streams and metadata.

packages.name: conventional_commit
packages.description: Parse a git commit message using the Conventional Commits specification.
packages.oneLiner: Parse a git commit message using the Conventional Commits specification.

explainer.whatItDoes: Parses git commit messages into structured data according to the Conventional Commits specification. It extracts components such as description, body, type, scopes, breaking changes, and footers.
useWhen: You are building changelog generation tools or release management utilities.
You need to validate commit messages against conventional commit standards in Dart or Flutter.
avoidWhen: You do not need to parse or validate git commit strings.
strengths: Provides a simple API for extracting all parts of a conventional commit message.
Handles edge cases like multi-line bodies, custom types, and breaking changes.
weaknesses: Very narrow and specialized scope.

packages.name: either_dart
packages.description: Error handler library for type-safe and easy work with errors on Dart and Flutter. Either is an alternative to Nullable value and Exceptions.
packages.oneLiner: Type‑safe Either monad for handling errors without exceptions in Dart/Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides Left/Right containers to represent failures and successes, with synchronous and asynchronous transformation methods. Includes extensions for Future<Either> to simplify async error handling.
useWhen: You need functional‑style error handling instead of try/catch
You want to chain async operations while propagating errors
You prefer explicit success/failure types over nullable values
avoidWhen: You require a full state‑management solution
You need built‑in networking or JSON serialization
strengths: Clear separation of error and success paths
Supports both sync and async pipelines
No external dependencies
weaknesses: Adds boilerplate of wrapping values in Either
Limited to error handling; not a full framework

alternatives.name: async
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides Future utilities but lacks explicit Either type for error handling

packages.name: webdev
packages.description: A CLI for Dart web development. Provides an easy and consistent set of features for users and tools to build and deploy web applications with Dart.
packages.oneLiner: A command-line tool for developing and deploying web applications with Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a local web development server with a file system watcher to rebuild on changes. Includes features for debugging web apps, launching in Chrome, and building applications for deployment.
useWhen: You are developing a web application with Dart.
You need a local development server with file watching and automatic rebuilds.
avoidWhen: You are building non-web Dart applications (like mobile or desktop).
You want to use it as a library dependency instead of activating it globally.
strengths: Integrates debugging features and DevTools support for Dart web apps.
Supports automatic page refresh and module reloading.
weaknesses: Not meant to be used as a package dependency, must be globally activated.
Requires specific build_runner and build_web_compilers setup.
explainer.setupNotes: Activate globally using `dart pub global activate webdev` and configure dev_dependencies like build_runner and build_web_compilers in pubspec.yaml.
explainer.example:
dart pub global activate webdev
webdev serve

packages.name: flutter_modular
packages.description: Smart project structure with dependency injection and route management for Flutter.
packages.oneLiner: Modular route management and dependency injection organized by feature.

explainer.whatItDoes: Flutter Modular organizes Flutter applications into feature-based modules, combining route management and dependency injection. It allows scoping dependencies and routes per feature, supporting named routes, nested routers, and route guards.
useWhen: You want to structure a large-scale Flutter application by features or modules.
You need nested routing with persistent shells using RouterOutlet.
You want integrated dependency injection tied to route lifecycles.
avoidWhen: You are building a tiny app where a standard MaterialApp navigation setup is sufficient.
You prefer completely decoupled state management and routing solutions.
strengths: Combines dependency injection and routing cleanly into modules.
Automatic disposal of page-scoped state tied to route lifecycles.
Supports dynamic parameters, submodules, and route guards.
weaknesses: Opinionated structure that requires adopting its module pattern across the app.
Ground-up rewrite in v7 may require migration effort from older versions.
explainer.setupNotes: Wrap your root widget with ModularApp and configure MaterialApp.router to use the routerConfig.

alternatives.name: get_it
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need standalone dependency injection without coupling to a specific routing architecture.

packages.name: custom_sliding_segmented_control
packages.description: Allows you to flexibly configure the widget for displaying controls. You can add color, speed, size, initial value, animation and more.
packages.oneLiner: A custom sliding segmented control widget with flexible configuration and animations.

explainer.whatItDoes: Allows you to build and customize a sliding segmented control widget with configurable colors, animation duration, curves, sizes, and initial values. It supports custom decorations for both the main panel and the sliding thumb.
useWhen: You need a custom segmented control with smooth sliding animations between options.
You want to style both the background container and the active segment thumb independently using BoxDecoration.
avoidWhen: You require standard platform-native segmented controls without custom styling.
You need complex navigation routing tied directly to the tabs.
strengths: Highly configurable decorations for both container and thumb
Supports custom animation curves and durations
Dynamic initial values and size calculations on orientation change
weaknesses: Limited documentation on advanced properties beyond the basic README example
Relies entirely on custom UI implementation rather than native look-and-feel bindings

packages.name: dcli
packages.description: Dart console SDK - write console (cli) apps/scripts using dart.
packages.oneLiner: A Dart SDK for building cross‑platform command line applications and scripts.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides APIs for creating CLI tools, handling arguments, I/O, compilation to native executables, and remote deployment. Includes utilities like ask, file handling, and system interactions.
useWhen: You need to write a Dart based CLI tool or script.
You want to compile Dart scripts into single‑file executables.
Cross‑platform console apps are required (Windows, macOS, Linux).
avoidWhen: You only need simple shell commands without a Dart runtime.
You require a GUI or Flutter widget library.
strengths: Cross‑platform support with native compilation.
Rich set of console utilities (prompt, file ops, permissions).
Integrates with Dart's ecosystem and null‑safety.
weaknesses: Relies on Dart SDK; adds size overhead for compiled binaries.
Limited to console use; not suitable for UI or web.

alternatives.name: win32
alternatives.why_pick_it: For low‑level Windows‑specific console or system calls without the full dcli abstraction.

packages.name: blur
packages.description: Blur is a wrapper widget that blur it's child. There are ImageBlur.asset and ImageBlur.network that blur the image. Frost is another wrapper which blurs the background.
packages.oneLiner: A wrapper widget and extension to blur children and images or apply frosted glass effects.

explainer.whatItDoes: Blur provides widgets and extensions to easily apply blur effects to any child widget, load and blur asset or network images, and create frosted glass background effects.
useWhen: You want to apply a blur effect to any widget or image easily.
You need frosted glass background effects in your UI.
avoidWhen: You need advanced image manipulation or caching capabilities.
strengths: Simple extension methods for widgets and images.
Supports frosted glass effects over backgrounds.
weaknesses: Limited to blurring tasks without deeper image processing features.

alternatives.name: image
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need comprehensive image decoding, manipulation, and processing instead of just a UI blur wrapper.

explainer.example:
Blur(
  blur: 2.5,
  blurColor: Theme.of(context).primaryColor,
  child: Padding(
    padding: EdgeInsets.all(8.0),
    child: Text('Blur'),
  ),
)

packages.name: sembast_web
packages.description: NoSQL persistent embedded database for the Web on top of IndexedDB
packages.oneLiner: NoSQL persistent embedded database for the Web on top of IndexedDB.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a NoSQL embedded database implementation for web applications using IndexedDB as the underlying storage. It supports cross-tab synchronization and transactions.
useWhen: You need a NoSQL embedded database specifically for Flutter Web or browser applications.
You want data to synchronize across multiple open browser tabs.
avoidWhen: You are looking for a relational SQL database solution.
You require built-in data encryption via codecs (which are not supported).
strengths: Content and transactions are synchronized across all open browser tabs.
Supports both JS and WASM targets.
weaknesses: Codecs are not supported on the web.
Transactions must be idempotent because they may run again in case of concurrent access.
explainer.setupNotes: Add sembast_web to your pubspec.yaml dependencies.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: Alternative NoSQL database for Flutter and Dart.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simpler key-value storage alternative if a full NoSQL database is overkill.

packages.name: emoji_regex
packages.description: emoji-regex offers a regular expression to match all emoji symbols and sequences (including textual representations of emoji) as per the Unicode Standard.
packages.oneLiner: Provides a regular expression to match all emoji symbols and sequences as per the Unicode Standard.

explainer.whatItDoes: It offers a regular expression designed to match all emoji symbols and sequences, including textual representations of emojis according to the Unicode Standard. The package is migrated from the npm emoji-regex library.
useWhen: You need to detect or extract emojis from text strings in Dart or Flutter.
You want to keep emoji-matching logic synchronized with the Unicode Standard.
avoidWhen: You only need to match a very small, fixed subset of emojis.
You need complex text parsing beyond simple regular expression matching.
strengths: Matches all emoji symbols and sequences according to the Unicode Standard.
Zero dependencies and lightweight.
weaknesses: Provides a single feature (regular expression matching) which could also be written manually if needed.
Not documented beyond basic description.
explainer.example: not documented

packages.name: result_dart
packages.description: Result for dart. It is an implementation based on Kotlin Result and Swift Result.
packages.oneLiner: Kotlin and Swift inspired Result class for error handling in Dart and Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Result and AsyncResult implementation to encapsulate success or failure values, reducing the need for try-catch blocks. Includes operators like map, flatMap, fold, and recover for transforming and handling outcomes.
useWhen: You want to return success or failure states cleanly without throwing exceptions.
You need functional error handling operators like map, flatMap, and fold.
You are writing asynchronous functions that can fail and want to use AsyncResult.
avoidWhen: Your architecture heavily relies on throwing and catching exceptions across the entire codebase.
You already use another functional programming package with its own comprehensive Either or Result type like dartz or fpdart.
strengths: Reduces boilerplate by defaulting failure types to Exception.
Includes a wide range of transformation and recovery operators.
Supports asynchronous workflows via AsyncResult typedef.
weaknesses: Does not provide full functional programming suites like dartz or fpdart.
Requires adopting a Result return type convention throughout the codebase.

packages.name: native_toolchain_cmake
packages.description: A library to invoke and build CMake projects for Dart Native Assets.
packages.oneLiner: A library to invoke and build CMake projects for Dart Native Assets.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides utilities to invoke and build CMake projects specifically for Dart Native Assets. Allows configuring CMake and Ninja versions, as well as Android NDK discovery through pubspec.yaml hooks.
useWhen: You are building Dart Native Assets that require compiling a CMake project.
You need to configure custom CMake, Ninja, or Android NDK versions for your native builds via pubspec.yaml.
avoidWhen: Your project does not use Dart Native Assets or CMake.
You want an established, stable toolchain library and wish to avoid experimental features.
strengths: Simplifies integrating CMake projects into Dart Native Assets workflows.
Supports fine-grained configuration for Android, iOS, Windows, Linux, and macOS in pubspec.yaml.
weaknesses: Explicitly marked as experimental and may change without warning.
Relies on external tools like CMake and Ninja being properly configured or discoverable.
explainer.setupNotes: Requires configuring hooks and user defines in pubspec.yaml, along with having CMake and Ninja or appropriate NDK paths set up for target platforms.
explainer.example:
hooks:
  user_defines:
    YOUR_PACKAGE_NAME:
      cmake_version: "3.22.1"
      ninja_version: "1.10.2"

packages.name: i18next
packages.description: A localization formatter based on the i18next standard. It is not yet a fully i18n tool only the formatting itself.
packages.oneLiner: A localization formatter and parser based on the i18next standard for Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Brings the i18next standard into Dart and Flutter applications. It handles variables, namespaces, contexts, plurals, fallbacks, and formatting within translation files.
useWhen: You are migrating an existing web or backend project using i18next to Flutter
You prefer the i18next syntax for interpolation, nesting, plurals, and contexts
avoidWhen: You want a fully-fledged zero-boilerplate code-generation solution like slang
You require features not yet supported such as resource caching or retrieving files directly from a server
strengths: Supports plural and context fallbacks, namespaces, and nested keys
Integrates smoothly with Flutter's LocalizationsDelegate and AssetBundle data sources
weaknesses: Pre-1.0.0 package with potential for frequent breaking changes
Missing some advanced features like sprintf support and resource caching
explainer.setupNotes: Declare the dependency in pubspec.yaml and register I18NextLocalizationDelegate in your MaterialApp or CupertinoApp.

alternatives.name: easy_localization
alternatives.why_pick_it: More mature and widely used localization package for Flutter with JSON/YAML support.

alternatives.name: slang
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides type-safe translations through code generation.

alternatives.name: intl
alternatives.why_pick_it: The official Dart localization library supporting standard ICU message formatting.

packages.name: calendar_view
packages.description: A Flutter package allows you to easily implement all calendar UI and calendar event functionality.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter package providing multiple calendar views and event management functionality.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides Month, Day, and Week calendar views with support for managing events, reminders, and full-day events. Allows high customization of UI components and syncing event data between multiple views.
useWhen: You need to implement fully customizable calendar views like Month, Day, and Week views in your app.
You want to manage calendar events, reminders, and multi-day events with event data synchronization.
You need built-in localization, RTL support, and dark theme support for calendars.
avoidWhen: You only need a simple date picker instead of full calendar grids and event scheduling.
You want a zero-configuration calendar widget with no custom event management logic.
strengths: Multiple built-in calendar view options (Month, Day, Week)
Comprehensive event, reminder, and multi-day event management
Highly customizable UI components, builders, and dark theme support
weaknesses: Releases in the 2.x.x range may introduce breaking changes requiring exact version pinning
Does not include built-in cloud backend syncing for events out of the box
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml. Pin the exact version (e.g. 2.0.0) as recommended to avoid breaking changes.

alternatives.name: table_calendar
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you need a widely-used calendar widget focused primarily on a highly customizable table layout and event markers.

explainer.example:
dependencies:
  calendar_view: 2.0.0

packages.name: locale_sweep
packages.description: A CI quality gate for Flutter localization. Runs app flows across locales, device sizes, text scales, and RTL modes, then reports broken screens with screenshot proof.
packages.oneLiner: A CI quality gate for Flutter localization testing across locales, viewports, and scales.

explainer.whatItDoes: Runs app flows across multiple locales, text scales, device sizes, and RTL modes to report broken layouts, missing keys, and text overflows with screenshot proof.
useWhen: You want to automate localization QA and catch text overflows before shipping.
You need to test your app across different locales, text scales, and RTL layouts automatically.
avoidWhen: You are not using localization in your Flutter app.
You do not write widget or integration tests.
strengths: Tests multiple variants (locales, scales, viewports, dark mode) from a single test call.
Catches text overflows, missing ARB keys, and placeholder mismatches.
Provides screenshot diffing and regression reports.
weaknesses: Relies on golden tests and screenshot comparisons, which can be brittle across different host operating systems.
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency as a dev_dependency, write a sweep test calling sweepTest, and generate initial golden baselines using dart run locale_sweep update.

packages.name: firebase_ui_localizations
packages.description: Localization package for firebase_ui_auth, firebase_ui_firestore and firebase_ui_database
packages.oneLiner: Localization package for Firebase UI auth, firestore, and database components.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides localization strings and translation management tooling for Firebase UI widgets. It includes commands to add new translation labels and generate localizations from ARB files.
useWhen: You are using Firebase UI packages in your Flutter app and need localized strings.
You want to add or modify translations for Firebase UI components using ARB files.
avoidWhen: You are not using any Firebase UI packages.
You need general app localization completely unrelated to Firebase.
strengths: Seamlessly integrates with Firebase UI components.
Includes developer tools like `add_label` and `gen_l10n` for managing translations.
weaknesses: Strictly scoped to Firebase UI packages.
Requires maintaining `.arb` files and running generators for custom languages.
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency and use standard Flutter localization delegates for Firebase UI.
explainer.example: dart run firebase_ui_localizations:gen_l10n

packages.name: jaspr
packages.description: A modern web framework for building websites in Dart that feels like Flutter but supports server-side rendering.
packages.oneLiner: A web framework for building websites in Dart with Flutter-like syntax and server-side rendering.

explainer.whatItDoes: Jaspr allows developers to build web applications using a component model that feels like Flutter, supporting both client-side and server-side rendering, automatic state syncing, and optimized DOM updates.
useWhen: You want to build websites in Dart with a Flutter-like component model.
You need server-side rendering (SSR) for web applications written in Dart.
You prefer writing web layouts using component composition and HTML element components.
avoidWhen: You are building a standard mobile or desktop application rather than a website.
You require a vast out-of-the-box library of pre-styled Material or Cupertino components.
strengths: Familiar component model for Flutter developers.
Built-in server-side rendering and automatic state sync between server and client.
Optimized DOM updates and CLI tool support with hot reloading.
weaknesses: Does not include pre-styled Material or Cupertino components.
Styling relies on CSS/stylesheets rather than property-based widget styling.
explainer.setupNotes: Activate the jaspr_cli globally and use `jaspr create` to scaffold a new project.

packages.name: extension_google_sign_in_as_googleapis_auth
packages.description: A bridge package between google_sign_in and googleapis_auth, to create Authenticated Clients from google_sign_in user credentials.
packages.oneLiner: Creates googleapis_auth AuthClient from GoogleSignIn credentials.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides an extension method that converts a GoogleSignIn authorization into a googleapis_auth AuthClient. The client can be used with googleapis package APIs to make authenticated calls.
useWhen: You need to call Google APIs (e.g., People API) after a user signs in with Google Sign‑In.
You want to avoid manually handling OAuth token exchange and refresh logic.
avoidWhen: You only need basic Google Sign‑In without accessing other Google APIs.
You prefer a custom OAuth flow or another authentication provider.
strengths: Bridges two official Flutter packages seamlessly.

Low CPU, GPU, and memory load compared to alternative players.

packages.name: squadron
packages.description: Multithreading and worker thread pool for Dart / Flutter, to offload CPU-bound and heavy I/O tasks to Isolate or Web Worker threads.
packages.oneLiner: Multithreading and worker thread pools for Dart and Flutter using Isolates and Web Workers.

explainer.whatItDoes: Squadron provides persistent worker pools and an abstraction layer to offload CPU-bound and heavy I/O tasks to background threads across platforms (Native Isolates and Web Workers). It handles type safety, task cancellation, streaming return types, and exception marshalling via code generation.
useWhen: You need to offload CPU-intensive tasks from the main thread without blocking UI performance.
You need persistent worker pools that stay alive across multiple tasks rather than spawning new isolates repeatedly.
You target both native (Dart VM) and browser platforms with a uniform multithreading API.
avoidWhen: Your app only requires simple one-off background tasks where `Isolate.run()` is sufficient and lightweight.
You want to avoid using code generation steps during development.
strengths: Cross-platform support for native Isolates and Web Workers (JS & WASM).
Persistent worker pools for handling frequent tasks efficiently.
Type-safe proxy generation and native Stream support from workers.
weaknesses: Requires code generation (`build_runner` and `squadron_builder`).
Requires manual worker lifecycle management (must call `stop()` to clean up background threads).
explainer.setupNotes: Add squadron to dependencies and squadron_builder / build_runner to dev_dependencies. Run build_runner to generate workers, and compile workers to JS/WASM for web targets.

HitScope(
  child: Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
    child: HitLayer(
      alignment: Alignment.center,
      behavior: HitTestBehavior.deferToChild,
      hitChild: GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onTap: () {},
        child: const SizedBox(width: 48, height: 48),

      paintChild: const IgnorePointer(

)

strengths: Reduces boilerplate for standard request-response and pagination flows.
Built-in request deduplication, caching, and refresh support.
Global configuration provider for default loaders, error widgets, and request modes.
weaknesses: Tied strictly to the bloc/cubit state management pattern.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides foundational state management primitives without specific request/pagination cubit wrappers.

)

useWhen: You are using the official video_player package and want a smooth, high-framerate progress bar or slider
You need more accurate time displays or animations tied to video playback position
avoidWhen: You are using an alternative video player library that is not video_player
You do not want a dependency on flutter_hooks

Only works with the standard video_player controller

explainer.example:
SmoothVideoProgress(
  controller: controller,
  builder: (context, position, duration, child) => Slider(
    onChangeStart: (_) => controller.pause(),
    onChangeEnd: (_) => controller.play(),
    onChanged: (value) =>
        controller.seekTo(Duration(milliseconds: value.toInt())),
    value: position.inMilliseconds.toDouble(),
    min: 0,
    max: duration.inMilliseconds.toDouble(),

);

explainer.whatItDoes: Nes UI provides a complete set of retro-styled widgets like buttons, checkboxes, containers, and dialogs. It includes a custom ThemeData and integrates with Google Fonts to deliver an 8-bit video game aesthetic.
useWhen: You are building a game UI or a retro-themed application in Flutter.
You want custom pixel-art styled widgets like NesButton, NesContainer, and NesConfirmDialog.
avoidWhen: You require standard Material or Cupertino look and feel.
You want a heavy focus on animations or physics-based motion without retro styling.
strengths: Distinct retro video game aesthetic out of the box.
Custom widgets designed specifically for retro game layouts and menus.
weaknesses: Limited to a very specific retro visual style.
Font loading via Google Fonts requires internet access at runtime unless bundled manually.
explainer.setupNotes: Call WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized() at the main method and add the flutterNesTheme() to your MaterialApp.

packages.oneLiner: Production-focused Flutter utilities for notifications, storage, connectivity, and media.

explainer.whatItDoes: A comprehensive utility package providing pre-configured services for push and local notifications, secure storage, Hive CE, connectivity checking, validation, and media/file pickers. It bundles common everyday extensions and helpers for production apps.
useWhen: You are building a production Flutter app and want a pre-packaged set of utilities for notifications, storage, and common validations.
You need an integrated solution for push/local notifications with deep-link handling and per-category mute preferences.
avoidWhen: You only need a single lightweight utility (like url_launcher or crypto) and want to avoid pulling in a large dependency graph.
Your project does not use Flutter 3.47+ or Dart 3.13+.
strengths: Combines many essential production utilities into a single, cohesive package.
Built-in support for per-category notification mute, cold-start taps, and in-app notification overlays.
Type-safe Result and AsyncState types for robust error handling.
weaknesses: Large dependency footprint due to covering multiple domains (storage, media, notifications, location).
Strict minimum requirement of Flutter 3.47 and Dart 3.13.
explainer.setupNotes: Requires initialisation in main() before runApp and specific platform configurations for Firebase, permissions, and minimum SDK versions (Android minSdk 24, compileSdk 37).
